holidays.name: National Apple Day (UK)
holidays.description: A British celebration of apples in all their glory, with orchards, markets, and community groups hosting apple tastings, cider pressing, and heritage variety swaps. Expect an absurd number of apple varieties you have never heard of.
holidays.origin: Launched in 1990 by the charity Common Ground to celebrate Britain's orchards and the diversity of local apple varieties, which were disappearing as supermarkets favored a few types.
holidays.funFact: Britain once grew thousands of apple varieties, with names like 'Slack-ma-Girdle', 'Knobby Russet', and 'Bloody Ploughman'.

holidays.name: National Pumpkin Cheesecake Day
holidays.description: A dessert holiday devoted to the creamy, spiced mashup of two autumn favorites. Skip the pumpkin spice latte for a day and dive into a slice instead.
holidays.origin: An unofficial American food holiday, popularized through food-calendar websites and social media as fall baking season peaks.
holidays.funFact: Cheesecake dates back to ancient Greece, where it was reportedly served to athletes at the first Olympic Games in 776 BC.

holidays.name: Back to the Future Day
holidays.description: Fans of the time-traveling film trilogy celebrate the date Marty McFly and Doc Brown arrive in the future in Back to the Future Part II. Expect hoverboard memes, DeLorean sightings, and people yelling about 1.21 gigawatts.
holidays.origin: The date October 21, 2015 was the destination on the DeLorean's time circuits in the 1989 film, and fans have celebrated it ever since, with the movie's 2015 anniversary causing a global frenzy.
holidays.funFact: Universal Pictures even released a fake Jaws 19 trailer in 2015 to mark the occasion, referencing the film's joke poster for the shark sequel.

holidays.name: National Reptile Awareness Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate scaly, cold-blooded friends, from geckos and turtles to snakes and iguanas, and to learn about their care and conservation.
holidays.origin: An awareness observance promoted by reptile enthusiasts, herpetology groups, and pet communities to encourage responsible ownership and conservation education.
holidays.funFact: Some geckos can walk on ceilings because of microscopic hairs on their toes that use molecular forces to stick to surfaces.

holidays.name: Fortune Cookie Day (Unofficial Observance Around This Date)
holidays.description: A tribute to the crispy folded cookie containing vague wisdom and lucky numbers. Everyone gets to pretend a stranger in a bakery knows their future.
holidays.origin: Fortune cookies are widely associated with Chinese restaurants in the United States, but they actually trace their modern origins to Japanese-American bakers in California in the early 1900s.
holidays.funFact: Fortune cookies are rarely found in China, where many people view them as an American invention.
